tagline: Break it to understand it. Fix it to master it.
description: A 12-week guided path into web application security and bug bounty hunting. Built for beginners who want to find real vulnerabilities in real applications.
outcome: Hands-on bug hunting experience, a working methodology, and readiness for bug bounty programs or AppSec roles.

phases.title: Phase 1 — Web Fundamentals
phases.subtitle: Weeks 1–4 · Understand how the web actually works

items.title: How the Web Works
items.detail: HTTP requests/responses, cookies, sessions, and the client-server model.

items.title: Linux & Command Line Basics
items.detail: Navigate a terminal comfortably — every tool you'll use lives here.

items.title: OWASP Top 10 Overview
items.detail: The ten most critical web application security risks, explained simply.

items.title: Mini Project: Set Up Your Testing Lab
items.detail: Install Burp Suite and run DVWA or Juice Shop locally.

phases.title: Phase 2 — Core Vulnerabilities
phases.subtitle: Weeks 5–8 · Learn to find and exploit real bugs

items.title: SQL Injection
items.detail: Manipulate database queries through unsanitized input.

items.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
items.detail: Inject scripts that run in another user's browser — stored, reflected, DOM-based.

items.title: Authentication & Access Control Flaws
items.detail: Broken login flows, IDOR, and privilege escalation between users.

items.title: Mini Project: Full PortSwigger Labs Sprint
items.detail: Clear 10 labs across SQLi, XSS, and access control categories.

items.title: Recon & Enumeration
items.detail: Subdomain enumeration, tech stack fingerprinting, and attack surface mapping.

items.title: Reporting Like a Professional
items.detail: Write clear, reproducible vulnerability reports that get accepted, not closed.

items.title: Join Your First Bug Bounty Programs
items.detail: Start on beginner-friendly public programs with active triage teams.

items.title: Build a Public Writeup Portfolio
items.detail: Publish 2–3 disclosed or lab-based writeups to show your methodology.
